back: A policy of national economic self-sufficiency, pursued by Italy especially after sanctions in 1935-36.
The Fascist system of corporations bringing employers, workers and the state together, replacing independent unions.
The target of 90 lire to the pound set in the Battle for the Lira (1926-27); it made exports dearer.

front: What did the Battle for Grain achieve?
back: Wheat output rose and imports fell, but other crops suffered and bread was dearer.
The Istituto per la Ricostruzione Industriale (1933), which took over failing banks' holdings and gave the state a large share of industry.
The Opera Nazionale Dopolavoro, the Fascist leisure organisation offering cheap holidays and clubs for workers.

front: Why did Mussolini's economic policies fail to raise living standards?
back: They aimed at prestige and war preparation, wages were cut, bread was dearer and the Corporate State left workers without a voice.

front: How did the state respond to the Great Depression?
back: Public works, the IMI (1931) and the IRI (1933), wage cuts and work-sharing.

front: Why was the Battle for Land limited?
back: Only a small area was reclaimed (the Pontine Marshes were the showpiece) and the large estates of the south were untouched.
